traceability.notes:
Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION defines an ESLint rule to enforce traceability conventions in test files: file-level @supports annotations, story references in describe() strings, and [REQ-...] prefixes in test names, with configuration, framework support, integration, and documentation.
Implementation status against Acceptance Criteria: - File-Level Annotations: Implemented via ensureFileSupportsAnnotation, which reports 'missingFileSupports' when no @supports is present in a detected test file and (optionally) auto-inserts a placeholder @supports JSDoc. Tested in tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts invalid case for missing @supports. - Describe Block Story References: Implemented via handleDescribeCall using a configurable describePattern (default 'Story [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+-') and messageId 'missingDescribeStory'. Tested in invalid case with describe('no story reference here', ...). - Test Name Requirement Prefixes: Implemented via handleItOrTestCall enforcing /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/ on it()/test() names, with safe normalization of malformed prefixes in --fix mode. Tested in cases for missing prefix and several malformed formats. - Quality Standards: Rule uses standard ESLint RuleModule shape, declares meta.schema, messages, and fixable, and limits work to files that match simple testFilePatterns with straightforward AST traversal. No performance issues are evident, and behavior is covered by dedicated tests. - Integration: The rule is dynamically loaded and exported by the plugin (src/index.ts), included in recommended and strict presets at severity 'error', and is asserted in tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts. README and user-docs describe it as part of the core rule set. - Error Messages: Messages exactly match those outlined in the story's example error messages and provide clear, actionable guidance. Additional context (e.g., TODO comments) is provided in the auto-inserted @supports template. - Framework Support: The helper recognizes 'describe', 'it', 'test', and 'context' as test framework calls, covering typical Jest and Mocha BDD patterns. Tests include 'context(...)' usage to validate non-Jest frameworks. - Documentation: user-docs/api-reference.md contains a detailed section for traceability/require-test-traceability, including description, all configuration options, behavior notes, and examples, and the rule is also referenced in README.md.
The story’s additional requirements about validating that @supports references existing story files and requirements are satisfied via composition with existing rules from dependency stories (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference), which already run on annotations in test files. Overall, all explicit acceptance criteria for Story 020.0 are met, with concrete implementation, tests, plugin integration, and documentation in place.
